qt: to the Commission Giuseppe Antoci (The Left) Subject:

The fruit and vegetable market in Vittoria (Sicily) is one of the main European hubs for the marketing of fruit and vegetables and plays a strategic role for the EU’s agri-food sectors. Over the years, investigative and judicial activities have highlighted the risk of organised crime infiltrating the fruit and vegetable sector, transport and logistics. Recent information has also highlighted the possible use of commercial and logistical networks related to this hub for transnational illicit trafficking, including drug trafficking1. In the light of the European Union’s objective of combating organised crime and protecting the integrity of the internal market and EU financial interests: 1.

Is the Commission aware of the risks of organised crime infiltrating the main European agri-food hubs, with particular reference to the Vittoria market, and does it consider it appropriate to assess the impact on the internal market?

Does it consider the monitoring tools and conditionality instruments to be up to the job of ensuring EU funds, in particular those under the common agricultural policy and cohesion policy, are not paid out to businesses affected by disqualifications or infiltrated by organised crime?

Will it consider taking further EU initiatives to prevent this infiltration, by strengthening cooperation between the Member States, Europol, Eurojust and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office and checks on the traceability of supply chains and the security of commercial logistics?

If these risks materialised, there would be serious consequences for competition, the protection of honest economic operators, the safety of agri-food chains and the protection of the EU’s financial interests. 1
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.10.2026) The Commission is aware of the infiltration into the legal economy by organised crime, as highlighted in Europol’s1 2025 Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment2 and 2026 report Decoding the EU’s Most Threatening Criminal Networks3. These indicate that 85% of these networks exploit legal businesses, including in transport, import and export. Under cohesion policy and the common agricultural policy, Member States must apply exclusion criteria, controls and effective penalties, while the Commission supervises and audits national control systems and can support risk detection through tools such as Arachne. The Commission also operates the Early Detection and Exclusion System, which allows persons and entities involved in serious misconduct, including organised crime, to be temporarily excluded from EU funding procedures without a final conviction. Crimes affecting the financial interests of the EU are investigated and prosecuted by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO). Moreover, the EU’s anti-fraud architecture to strengthen protection against evolving threats, including transnational organised crime, will be reviewed, with a Communication envisaged for December 2026. The Commission will present, in early 2027, a proposal on organised crime (including an Impact Assessment examining, inter alia, effects of organised crime on the Internal Market) to strengthen the response to criminal networks and their infiltration of the legal economy, also through modernised participation offenses and stronger cross-border cooperation. In 2026, the Commission also adopted two proposals revising the Europol and Eurojust4 Regulations5 aimed at strengthening cross-border investigations and cooperation with the EPPO.
1 European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation. 2 Europol (2025), European Union Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment – The changing DNA of

serious and organised crime, Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg, p. 27. 3 Europol (2026), Decoding the EU’s most threatening criminal networks - Issue 2: The blueprint of criminal opportunism, Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg, p. 42. 4 European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation. 5 COM(2026) 580 final, COM(2026) 570 final.
